correctness.rationale: For every positive parameter vector the homogeneous conic is three-side tangent and elliptic; exact quadratic-matrix determinant and center value yield the normalized area. Point containment is exactly the triangle inequality for \(\sqrt{u_iw_i}\). The feasibility set is convex because the geometric mean is concave, and logarithmic area is strictly concave. Outside the Steiner ellipse the single initially violated triangle inequality is active; all other inequalities are strict on that boundary. The boundary product reduces to one rational function with a cubic derivative having exactly one positive zero by Descartes and endpoint signs. This proves global uniqueness and the area formula for all interior targets. The median specialization and its one-sided second derivatives were independently symbolically checked; bundled exact-rational and deterministic randomized checks replay successfully. No computational sample is used to infer the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The complete constrained maximum-area profile for a marked interior point, the unique positive-root cubic, and the sharp median saturation law were not stated by the inspected primary sources. This is not an originality claim for the classical unrestricted Steiner maximizer, its area formula, or the standard inellipse parametrizations. Comparisons use implication and exact feasible-set distinctions; specialist historical priority remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Specialized pre-2016 or classical projective-geometry treatments may already optimize a triangle inellipse through or containing a marked point under different terminology; absence from search results cannot establish priority.

value.rationale: The input is an arbitrary triangle and an arbitrary interior point; the exact area of the largest three-side-tangent ellipse containing it is a natural target-constrained geometric extremum, not an arbitrary slice. The result gives a complete affine-invariant classification, a constructive positive-root cubic, and a sharp geometric saturation boundary at the Steiner inellipse. The exact median law exhibits a nontrivial second-derivative jump. These supply explicit geometric design information not determined by the classical unconstrained Steiner optimality alone.
